get_current_matchday.description: Find which round a league is on right now. This is the one action that needs no season: OpenLigaDB works out which season is running and which round of it is next, which is what a weekly digest needs before it can ask for the fixtures. No API key required.
get_current_matchday.name: get_current_matchday

parameters.description: The competition to read, picked from every league OpenLigaDB holds. The list is ordered with the long running competitions first, so the Bundesliga, its lower tiers and the DFB-Pokal are near the top.
parameters.name: league

found.description: True when the league is between or during matchdays. False when it is not running at all, which is a normal answer out of season.

label.description: The same round in English, e.g. Matchday 1.

league.description: The league shortcut the answer is about.

name.description: The round's name in German, e.g. 1. Spieltag.

get_group_tables.description: Get the standings of a tournament that plays in groups, one table per group, as at a World Cup or a European Championship. Only a competition with a group stage has these; a league that plays one table answers with a message pointing at Get the league table. No API key required.
get_group_tables.name: get_group_tables

parameters.description: The competition to read, picked from every league OpenLigaDB holds. The list is ordered with the long running competitions first, so the Bundesliga, its lower tiers and the DFB-Pokal are near the top.
parameters.name: league

parameters.description: Which season of that league. A season is named for the year it starts in, so 2025 is the 2025/2026 season. The list shows only the seasons this league actually has.
parameters.name: season

count.description: How many rows are in this page.

groups.description: The groups, each with its own table.

count.description: How many teams are in it.

table.description: The table, best placed team first.

icon_url.description: The team's crest, as a URL.

position.description: Where the team sits in the table, counting from 1. This is the order OpenLigaDB ranked them in, so a competition with its own tie-breaking rules keeps them.

league.description: The league shortcut the answer is about.

season.description: The season the answer is about.

team_count.description: How many teams there are across every group.

get_head_to_head.description: Get every match two teams have played against each other, with the record worked out: how many each has won, how many were drawn, and the goals either way. OpenLigaDB answers with their whole shared history across every competition it holds, and fixtures still to come are included alongside. No API key required.

parameters.name: season

parameters.description: One of the two teams. The record is reported from this team's point of view.
parameters.name: team_1

parameters.description: The other team. It must be a different one.
parameters.name: team_2

parameters.description: Optional. Keep only matches in these states. A match counts as in progress once its kick-off has passed and OpenLigaDB has not yet marked it finished. Choose none to keep them all.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Optional. Return the latest kick-off first instead of the earliest. Off by default, which is fixture-list order.
parameters.name: newest_first

parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Optional. How many rows to skip before this page. Use the next offset from the previous result to page through. 0 by default.

count.description: How many rows are in this page.

has_more.description: True when more rows matched than this page holds.

league.description: The league the teams were picked from, which does not limit the meetings returned.

items.description: One match, with its score, its stage scores and its goals.

goal_count.description: How many goals are listed below.

goals.description: Every goal in the match, in the order they were scored.

comment.description: Whatever note was recorded with the goal, e.g. '+11' for the eleventh minute of stoppage time. Usually null.

is_overtime.description: True for a goal in stoppage time or extra time rather than inside the ninety.

minute.description: The minute it was scored. Null when OpenLigaDB was not told one.

score_team1.description: The home side's running score after this goal.

score_team2.description: The away side's running score after this goal.

scorer_name.description: The scorer, usually as an initial and a surname, e.g. F. Wirtz.

scoring_team_id.description: The team credited with the goal. For an own goal this is the team that benefited.

goals_team1.description: The home side's goals at the last stage recorded. Null before anything has been entered.

goals_team2.description: The away side's goals at the last stage recorded.

half_time_team1.description: The home side's goals at half-time, when it was recorded.

half_time_team2.description: The away side's goals at half-time, when it was recorded.

is_finished.description: True once OpenLigaDB has marked the match finished.

kickoff_local.description: The same kick-off in the venue's local time, with no zone attached. For display next to the time zone below.

last_update.description: When OpenLigaDB last changed this match, on its own clock and with no time zone attached.

league_id.description: The numeric id of the league season the match belongs to. Every action here is addressed by shortcut and season instead.

league_name.description: The league's full name, e.g. 1. Fussball-Bundesliga 2024/2025.

league_season.description: The season, named for the year it starts in, e.g. 2024.

location_city.description: The venue's city. Null when none was entered.

location_id.description: OpenLigaDB's id for the venue. Null when none was entered.

location_stadium.description: The stadium's name. Null when none was entered.

match_id.description: OpenLigaDB's id for the match. Get a match takes one of these.

matchday.description: Which round of the season the match is in, counting from 1.

matchday_label.description: The same round in English, e.g. Matchday 1 or Quarter-final. A round whose name has no English equivalent keeps the original.

matchday_name.description: The round's name as OpenLigaDB stores it, e.g. 1. Spieltag.

matchday_url.description: The page on openligadb.de showing this round's matches.

number_of_viewers.description: The attendance, when a contributor recorded one. Null for most matches.

results.description: The score at each stage the match was recorded at: half-time, after ninety minutes, and after extra time or penalties when it went that far.

description.description: OpenLigaDB's own longer note on the stage, in German.

kind.description: The stage as a stable code: HalfTime, After90Minutes, AfterExtraTime, AfterPenalties or Unknown. Branch on this rather than on the German name.

label.description: The same stage in English, e.g. Half-time or Full-time.

name.description: The stage's name as OpenLigaDB stores it, in German, e.g. Halbzeit.

order.description: Where the stage falls in the match: 1 is half-time, 2 is full time, and anything higher came after.

points_team1.description: The home side's score at this stage.

points_team2.description: The away side's score at this stage.

result_id.description: OpenLigaDB's id for this recorded score.

result_type_id.description: The result type this stage was recorded under.

score.description: The two goal counts as one string, e.g. 2:3. Null when there is no score yet.

score_source.description: Where the score came from: 'result' when OpenLigaDB has entered one, or 'goals' when the match is still being played and the running total after the last goal was used instead. Null when there is no score.

status.description: One of finished, live or upcoming. Live means the kick-off has passed and OpenLigaDB has not yet marked the match finished.

team1_icon_url.description: The home side's crest, as a URL that can be embedded.

team1_short_name.description: The home side's short name, e.g. Gladbach.

team2_icon_url.description: The away side's crest, as a URL that can be embedded.

team2_short_name.description: The away side's short name, e.g. Leverkusen.

time_zone_id.description: The Windows time zone the local kick-off is in, e.g. W. Europe Standard Time.

winner.description: Which side is ahead: team1, team2 or draw. Null when there is no score yet.

winner_name.description: The winning side's name. Null for a draw or no score.

winner_team_id.description: The winning side's team id. Null for a draw or no score.

next_offset.description: The offset that fetches the next page. Null when this is the last one.

played.description: How many of their meetings have been played. The record below counts only these.

season.description: The season the answer is about.

team_1_goals.description: Goals the first team has scored in them.

team_1_wins.description: How many the first team won.

team_2_goals.description: Goals the second team has scored in them.

team_2_wins.description: How many the second team won.

get_last_change_date.description: Find when a matchday's data last changed. This is the cheap check to run on a schedule: compare the answer with the one from the previous run and only fetch the matches when it has moved, rather than pulling a whole matchday every few minutes. Leave the matchday blank to watch whichever round the league is currently on. No API key required.

get_last_change_date.name: get_last_change_date

description: Pull German football results and fixtures into a workflow from OpenLigaDB, the open sports database behind the Bundesliga, its second and third tiers, the DFB-Pokal, the women's Bundesliga, national-team tournaments and hundreds of other competitions, ice hockey and handball among them. Read a matchday's scores goal by goal, a league's table, its scoring charts, one team's fixtures across every competition it plays in, or the record between two clubs. Check the next kick-off for a reminder, or watch a matchday for changes so a workflow only runs when something has actually happened. No account or API key required.
